_comment: Single source of truth for the method catalogue. The run wizard renders its forms from `params` here and the trainers validate against the same block, so a hyperparameter cannot exist in the UI without existing in the trainer.

rubric.label: Helpfulness
rubric.guidance: Does the response actually do what was asked, completely and at the right level of detail?

rubric.label: Accuracy
rubric.guidance: Is every factual claim correct and every instruction faithfully followed? Fabrication is disqualifying.

rubric.label: Style & tone
rubric.guidance: Is it clear, well-organised, and free of padding, hedging, and restatement of the question?

sft.label: Supervised fine-tuning
sft.blurb: Teach the base model your task from demonstration data. Start here — every preference method assumes a competent policy to improve.

params.name: epochs
params.label: Epochs
params.help: Passes over the training set. Small datasets need more; past ~5 epochs a LoRA starts memorising.

params.name: learning_rate
params.label: Learning rate
params.help: 2e-4 is the standard LoRA starting point — roughly 10x what you would use for a full fine-tune.

params.name: grad_accum
params.label: Gradient accumulation
params.help: Multiplies effective batch size without extra memory.

params.name: completion_only_loss
params.label: Train on completion only
params.help: Mask the prompt out of the loss. Off means the model also learns to produce your prompts, which is rarely what you want.

params.name: packing
params.label: Pack short examples
params.help: Concatenate examples up to max length. Faster on short data; blurs example boundaries.

reward.label: Reward model
reward.blurb: Bradley-Terry scorer trained on preference pairs. Required by PPO; optional elsewhere as an offline evaluator.

params.name: margin_weighting
params.label: Weight by preference margin
params.help: A 5-0 reviewer split should move the scorer further than a 3-2 split.

dpo.label: DPO — Direct Preference Optimization
dpo.blurb: Closed-form preference learning. No reward model, no sampling, no rollout loop: the most stable way to spend a set of preference pairs.

params.name: beta
params.label: Beta (KL strength)
params.help: How far the policy may drift from the reference. Lower = freer and less stable. 0.1 is the usual default.

params.name: learning_rate
params.label: Learning rate
params.help: An order of magnitude below SFT. DPO diverges loudly if this is too high.

params.name: label_smoothing
params.label: Label smoothing (cDPO)
params.help: Assume this fraction of preference labels are wrong. Useful with noisy crowd annotation.

params.name: sft_weight
params.label: Auxiliary SFT weight
params.help: Adds NLL on the chosen response (RPO). Counteracts DPO's tendency to lower both likelihoods.

ppo.label: PPO — Proximal Policy Optimization
ppo.blurb: The classic on-policy RLHF loop: sample, score with a reward model, update inside a trust region. Most powerful, most moving parts.

params.name: iterations
params.label: Iterations
params.help: Each iteration samples a batch of prompts, scores them, and takes `ppo_epochs` update passes.

params.name: kl_coef
params.label: KL penalty coefficient
params.help: Per-token penalty against the reference policy. The main guard against reward hacking.

params.name: target_kl
params.label: Target KL (adaptive)
params.help: 0 disables adaptation and holds the KL coefficient fixed.

grpo.label: GRPO — Group Relative Policy Optimization
grpo.blurb: PPO with the critic deleted. Samples a group per prompt and uses the group's own mean as the baseline — half the memory, no value-function bugs.

params.name: group_size
params.label: Group size (G)
params.help: Completions sampled per prompt. The baseline is their mean reward, so groups below ~4 give a noisy advantage.

params.name: mu
params.label: Update passes per batch
params.help: mu=1 is fully on-policy and makes the importance ratio exactly 1.

params.name: scale_by_std
params.label: Divide advantage by group std
params.help: Standard GRPO. Turning it off (Dr. GRPO) removes a bias that over-weights low-variance prompts.

gspo.label: GSPO — Group Sequence Policy Optimization
gspo.blurb: GRPO's fix for long generations: importance ratios and clipping move to the sequence level, so one freak token can no longer blow up an entire update.

params.name: mu
params.label: Update passes per batch
params.help: GSPO's reason to exist is tolerating off-policy passes, so mu>1 is where it pays off.

params.name: clip_low
params.label: Clip range (low)
params.help: Sequence ratios are length-normalised and hug 1.0 far more tightly than token ratios, so GSPO clips ~3 orders of magnitude tighter than PPO.

params.name: kl_coef
params.label: KL penalty coefficient
params.help: GSPO is usually run without an explicit KL term; sequence clipping already constrains the step.

rlaif.label: RLAIF — AI feedback
rlaif.blurb: Replaces the human labelling step, not the optimiser. A judge model ranks sampled candidates into preference pairs, then the pipeline you pick consumes them.

params.name: optimizer
params.label: Optimiser
params.help: AI feedback is the label source. This is what actually updates the weights.

params.name: position_debias
params.label: Score both orderings
params.help: Judges favour whichever answer they read first. Scoring A/B and B/A and averaging removes most of it — at double the cost.

params.name: min_margin
params.label: Minimum score margin
params.help: Discard pairs the judge could barely separate. Ties teach nothing and add gradient noise.

params.name: human_spot_check
params.label: Route a sample to human review
params.help: Fraction of judged pairs also queued for a human. This is what turns an unfalsifiable judge into a measured one.
